title: Original availability by industry and financial year, 2012-2025
question: Which industries drive the level of availability, which moved in 2022, and how large was the provider break per industry?
notes_text: Source: RFSD v3.1.0; lab aggregation of the foundation registry by released two-digit OKVED class and financial year. Cells show eligible records with an original statement as a percentage of eligible records; darker blue is higher on a 20 to 90 scale. Industries holding at least 1 percent of 2021 eligible records are listed; the remaining classes are pooled in one row and records with a missing class in another. The 2018 to 2019 change coincides with the Rosstat to FNS provider change and is a measurement break, not industry behaviour. 2011 has no original statements and is not shown; 2025 is the flagged latest year. Descriptive.
reading: A numbers-in-cells table: human health, engineering and software report most, membership organisations and transport support least, and the ordering is stable across years. The provider change lifted most industries by a few points but metal products by thirteen. Records without an industry class almost never carry an original statement.
caveats: Industries with at least 1 % of 2021 eligible records; the rest pooled
The 2018 to 2019 column is a measurement break
source_line: Foundation registry, lab aggregation by industry and year
